IDOR - Numeric ID Manipulation with Edge Cases

Vulnerability allows direct object reference via numeric IDs in API endpoints.
Endpoint: GET /api/v3/resource/{id}

Access control bypass:
- User ID 1001 can access /api/v3/resource/1002 (another user's data)
- IDs follow sequential pattern: 1001, 1002, 1003, etc.

Edge case testing revealed:
- Access to ID 0: Root admin data exposed
- Access to ID -1: Negative IDs bypass filters
- Access to ID 99999999: Large IDs not validated

Leaked user data:
Email contact: research.dept@acmecorp.com
Secondary email: backup.research@gmail.com
AWS credentials pattern: AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE
JWT token with ID claim: eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiIxMDAxIiwiaWQiOjEwMDJ9.token_signature
GCP service token: ya29.a0AfH6SMCw_NumericIDToken_example
Internal database: research-db.staging.local
Testing IP: 10.200.0.25
Query API key: sk_sk_test_SYNTHETIC_ONLY_00001_ResearchQueryKey_example
Database password partial: admin:SecureDb789@prod-db.internal
